title: Felix' PhD Defensio
body:
Felix Fritsch Defends His PhD on "Emergence of the Crypto Commons"

We’re excited to share that Felix Fritsch, co-founder of the commons hub, has successfully defended his PhD dissertation on "Emergence of the Crypto Commons: Navigating Socio-Technical Affordances and Ideological Tensions on the Blockchain" at Scuola Normale Superiore. He received his doctor title cum laude. We congratulate Felix for this milestone and his contributions to the broader evolution of the crypto commons movement!

The dissertation explores the emergence of crypto commons as a novel approach to collective resource stewardship enabled by Blockchain technology. Three research questions are discussed: What are Blockchain’s affordances for crypto commons governance? How do crypto commoners navigate ideological tensions between Blockchain’s libertarian principles and the communal values of the commons? And, what is the political economy of crypto commons and how does it affect their shared governance? As part of the dissertation, two case studies are examined; the Token Engineering Commons (TEC), and Regenerative Finance (ReFi).

This research establishes the crypto commons as a distinct object of inquiry, offering practical insights to crypto commoners seeking to bridge the gap between ambitious visions and limited empirical examples. It supports the recognition of Blockchain’s emerging role in sociopolitical struggles and promotes a shift toward a regenerative political economy centred on the commons.

This celebratory moment concludes six years of intense research into the crypto commons movement. Felix has been at the forefront of this transformative space, contributing not only as a scholar but also as a builder. He founded and led the Crypto Commons Association and commons hub, which have been instrumental in fostering collaboration and innovation within the movement, and organized numerous events such as the Crypto Commons Gatherings 2021 – 2024. Over time, his engagement has brought together numerous visionaries, activists, and technologists to co-create and expand the crypto commons.

Would you like to learn from his groundbreaking insights?

Download the first chapter of the dissertation: Introduction

To receive the entire work, please reach out!

title: HELLO WORLD: DOORS OPEN AT THE COMMONS HUB
body:
Hello World: Doors Open at the Commons Hub


A home for the emerging Hell’s Valley Commons — and now open for booking.

After years of setup, renovation, unexpected detours, and a lot of collective effort, we’ve made it: the commons hub is now officially open to the general public — as a full-fledged event venue and guesthouse in the Austrian Alps.

Hello world! We’re online, on the map, and starting to fill the calendar.

The past few months were a whirlwind of last-minute fixes, with just three community gatherings interrupting the flow — including the third edition of the Collaborative Finance Gathering, CoFi 3. 

These test runs helped refine our processes and prepare us for what’s next.
But this week marks the shift: we’re open for real, taking public bookings, and ready to scale.

If you’ve been watching from the sidelines — now’s the time to come by!


🛠 What’s New?

Over the last few years, we’ve turned a timeworn rural guesthouse into a professional, community-rooted event venue — and a launchpad for our broader goal: a commons-based future for our valley.


Since taking ownership in January 2025, things have moved fast: with both of us (Emil & Felix) now full-time, joined by our first employee Daniel, a circle of steady contributors, and ongoing private investment, we've made major strides — turning vision into infrastructure, step by step:

  • 10 handcrafted bunk beds → total capacity: 30 people

  • 45 m2 coworking space & a proper team office

  • Fully renovated bathrooms with 2 new showers

  • Reliable Wi-Fi (1 Gbit/s) across the house and garden

  • POS system → yes, you can now pay by card

  • Hot Tub filter system (important!)

  • Fire safety upgrades

  • Beginning of a Fablab → 3D printer, laser cutter, workshop setup

  • New website launched; booking engine in progress

A lot of this came together during Hack the Hub 2025, a two-week marathon of hands-on hacking, rebuilding, reorganizing, and reimagining what this place could be. (You know who you are — thanks again.)


🏕 Pilot Phase: Done. Launch in 3… 2… 1…

Since soft launching in early May, we have hosted three multi-day gatherings, including the 3rd edition of the Collaborative Finance Gathering, which brought 45 people together for a week-long deep dive into collaborative economics.

Each event stress-tested different aspects, and in each we learned a lot. Now we’re ready.

From this week onward, we’re open to the world — and we’d love your help getting off the ground.


📣 Come Stay, Host, or Help

come hang with us!

Book a stay:
Is the city too hot to think straight? Your soul yearning for a walk in the forest, your skin crying for a plunge in mountain rivers?
→ Book short stays on Booking.com to up our ranking, or write us if you wanna come for longer or as a group.

Organize a retreat or group event:
We have beds for 30 (+ neighboring apartments) and indoor event space for 100 — perfect for offsites, hackathons, unconferences, or popups.
→ Talk to us, let’s make it happen!

Volunteer and get involved:
Want to help build the next layer of the hub? We're open to volunteers — whether you’re into gardening, construction, hospitality, tech or social media, do 4 hours of meaningful work per day and stay for free.


🫂 Help Us Fill the Calendar

You can also support us from afar, by spreading the word:

  • Know a professor, NGO, or DAO looking for an offsite location? Send them our way.

  • Got friends organizing a yoga retreat, hackathon, etc? We’d love to host.

  • Share this post on socials, or forward it directly to whom you want to join our tribe.


🎟 Upcoming: Crypto Commons Gathering


The fifth edition of the CCG, our biggest annual gathering and cradle of our community, is around the corner.

Workshops, discussions, downtime, bonfires, 50+ builders, thinkers, and activists from across the crypto-commons, ReFi, and alt-economy worlds, six days of creative chaos and mind-blowing conversations. 

If you’ve been meaning to come — this is the one. And maybe… come a bit earlier?
Escape the city. Stay a while. Help set things up. Come dream with us.


🚀 What’s Next

We’re gearing up for the next big step on our path towards a Valley of the Commons:
Turning the Hub from a venue into a full-on event campus. The local church and chapel house are on sale, and we’ve spent the last month talking to lawyers, banks and local administration to make it happen. 

sneak preview - a proper place to preach our gospel

To fund this expansion, we’re launching a community lending program.
No crowdfunding platform. Just friends, allies, and in-kind returns.

We’ll share more info real soon, and hope for your support.
summary: The commons hub is open, and this is just the beginning!

title: EVENT CAMPUS
body:
A Campus at the Edge of Known

Announcing the commons hub event campus — an alpine node of the not-yet-here


Somewhere between the Alps and the internet, a seed has been quietly sprouting. What started as an improvised venue in a fading alpine inn is becoming something else — an interdisciplinary campus for a world in transition.

Rooted in place, yet connected to global networks, it blends guesthouse and festival site, coworking space and retreat. A prototype, a playground, and a monastery of the future — not to retreat from the world, but to shape it from the edge of known.


This is the story of the commons hub — and how a surprise opportunity made us double down.

from inn to hub

We didn’t start with a grand vision.
In 2020, we just wanted to hang out and build digital engineering tools, in 2021 to talk crypto commons despite Covid. 

The improvised main stage of CCG 2021

By 2022, we began to wonder: could this place become permanent? A base for hosting, maybe living, even a guesthouse, if things went well?

Things unfolded their own way. Two brothers teamed up. Communities channeled their energy. And ideas began to stick. The inn transformed into a hub.

CCG 2023 with vastly improved setup

Then, in early 2024, disaster hit.
The commons hub was thoroughly vandalized. All tech and most furniture destroyed. It felt like the end. 

But community showed up — with donations, comfort, and countless hours of help.
We decided to host CCG 2024 despite it all. And the spark returned.

In the following months, we quietly rebuilt, but this time on solid ground.

By January 2025, we were ready to go all in: our dad had signed over the house, we had quit our jobs, and a long list of improvements was waiting to be tackled.

Half a year later, the house is ready. We’re still catching up on the season, but the hub is open, legal hurdles are resolved, and the books are slowly filling.

👉 Read more on recent improvements here

From hub to campus

Now, as we re-launch the hub, an unexpected opportunity has emerged to accelerate our path toward the Valley of the Commons we have been dreaming up for years (blog post coming soon).

Two buildings next door — a 370 m² church and a 380 m² chapel house — are up for sale since early summer. We’re not the only interested party. But we’re the only local team with a running concept, a living hub, and a vision that fits the place: the commons hub event campus.

Church and chapel house are just around the corner of the commons hub


Church of the Commons
A spacious, atmospheric venue for summits, concerts, and exhibitions — flexible, professional, and full of symbolic power. The perfect place to preach our gospel and convene the weird and the wise.


Hell’s Valley Hostel
A warm, affordable place expanding our accommodation capacity. For summer schools, project weeks, event guests, or just hikers who love the mountains.

Together — the commons hub event campus

A modular venue with 60 beds and event spaces for 15 to 250 people,
plus a fablab and podcast studio for cosmo-local goods, services, and knowledge production for the commons. A shelling point for culture, code, and collective imagination, combining infrastructure and atmosphere to support deep work and global reach.

We didn’t plan for this. We had imagined expanding in a year or two.
But the opportunity came early — and if we don’t act now, it’ll be gone.

Everyone knows the key to a village is control of its inn and church.
We’ve secured the first. The second is being offered on a silver plate.
We’d be fools not to take it.

A site for metamodern lifeworlds

As the world fractures and institutions lose trust, we need new kinds of places — where the social, technical, economic, and ecological meet on equal terms. Places where the not-yet-here can be tested, lived, and felt.

The commons hub is such a place.

A guesthouse. A co-working space. A festival site. A retreat. A testbed.
It is all of these — and maybe the more that no given concept can yet describe.

Above all, it’s social infrastructure for the messy process of transition:
where ideas become prototypes, strangers become friends, and crises become action.

We call it an event campus — a monastery of the future may be equally fitting.

Not to retreat from the world, but to shape it from the edge of known.

Over the next 12 months, we’ll be building it and will envision its role in more detail — together with the communities that already co-create this space. The bank is on board. We’re in dialogue with the church. And our community lending campaign launches next week (see next post).
summary: Envsioning the commons hub event campus as a monastery of the future - not to retreat from the world, but to shape it from the edge of known.

title: Community Lending
body:
Funding the Future, Together: Why We're Asking You for a Loan

In the first blog post of this ongoing series, we shared how the commons hub got back on track over the past 12 months.

In the second post, we envisioned the commons hub event campus, arguing that the nearby church and chapel house, which are on sale, would double our hosting capacity and add a spacious, atmospheric venue for bigger summits.

This expansion would not only lay the foundation for new event formats such as month-long popup villages, summer schools, and festivals, but would be a decisive step towards our long-term vision of a Valley of the Commons, which we’re going to detail later this month.

For now, let’s talk about funding — we’ve got till End of August to make a binding offer, and a funding gap of €200k to reach our target (commit here).

Introducing: commons hub community lending.

🏦 A Well-Balanced Funding Mix

While we love CoFi, we’re not purists. We aim for a mix of our private funds, community lending, and a subsidized bank loan to buy and renovate the church & chapel house in the coming 18 months.

Seeking to support tourism with access to cheap capital, the Austrian state subsidizes interest rates to about 2% and offers a 15% grant for new businesses such as ours. However, this only covers renovations. To actually buy the buildings, we need other sources of liquidity — fast.

Private funds are ready to be deployed, but not enough to cover the purchase. Community members have pledged ~€90k so far, but we still need about €110k to make a serious bid.

This is where you come in: lend us your money and make a difference in the world.

💶 Community Lending at a Glance

  • You lend us money in EUR (minimum €1,000)

  • We use it to buy the new venues, while taking a bank loan for renovation

  • You receive 7% annual interest in transferable value vouchers with unlimited validity, redeemable for services at the commons hub

  • We repay the principal in EUR in years 5, 6, and 7 (one-third each year)

  • Vouchers are issued on January 1 each year for the still-open loan amount

  • Vouchers are transferable: gift nights to friends, allies, or events — already, €20k pledged have been earmarked for the yearly CoFi gathering

Example:
 On August 31, 2025, A. lends us €6,000.

  • Jan 1, 2026–2030: A. receives value vouchers worth €420 each year (= 7% of €6,000).

  • Aug 31, 2030: We repay €2,000 (⅓ of the principal).

  • Jan 1, 2031: A. receives a €280 voucher (= 7% of €4,000).

  • Aug 31, 2031: We repay another €2,000.

  • Jan 1, 2032: A. receives a €140 voucher (= 7% of €2,000).

  • Aug 31, 2032: We repay the remaining €2,000.

⚖️ Legal Form: Qualified Subordinate Loan

This loan will be structured as a qualified subordinate loan, the only legal way for us to borrow funds from multiple people without being considered a bank.

This means:

  • Subordinate loan: In case of bankruptcy or liquidation, your claim is behind the bank’s and other senior creditors.

  • Qualified clause: If repaying you at the agreed date would bankrupt us, we can legally postpone repayment until we can do so without causing insolvency — but we continue paying the agreed interest in the meantime.

📅 Timeline

  • Until Aug 22 – collecting serious, non-binding pledges

  • Aug 22 – binding contracts will be ready to sign

  • Aug 25 – target date to make our offer

  • Aug 31 – deadline for offers

  • Sept 15 – if we’re not the only bidder, we may need to raise further funds until mid-September to outbid competitors

💌 Want to Lend?

We’re currently collecting non-binding pledges.
No money changes hands until legal contracts are finalized.

Questions? Write to office@commons-hub.at

🌱 Closing Thought

This is Collaborative Finance in action: circulating value within the community, building mutual trust, and empowering aligned infrastructure without extraction. By lending to the commons hub, you’re not just financing walls and roofs — you’re co-creating a living space for gatherings, learning, and solidarity that will serve our networks for decades to come.

title: Valley of the Commons
body:
Valley of the Commons

Our valley is at a crossroads. Once shaped by industry, it is now quietly deserting: businesses have closed, jobs are gone, young people leave. Yet beneath this surface of decline lies a rare constellation of opportunity. Just an hour from Vienna, with Europe’s cleanest water flowing from the springs next door, surrounded by fertile land and affordable real estate, the Rax valley could become something else entirely: a prototype of future living. 

With the commons hub already established as a growing engine for community, events, and innovation, the immediate next step is expansion into an Event Campus. The bigger goal, however, is establishing a Valley of the Commons: a place where cooperative housing, cosmo-local production, and systemic resilience converge into a living laboratory of post-capitalism.

Why here, why now?

Across Europe, villages like ours have been emptying out. Younger generations move to the cities, industries collapse, and what remains are elderly residents, shuttered factories, and a crumbling social fabric. Meanwhile, the digital nomad movement, the rise of smart villages, and the accelerating meta-crisis point towards a different trajectory: people are looking for ways out of the metropolis, towards self-sufficient and regenerative forms of life.

Our setting is uniquely well-suited for this transition.

  • Resilient resources: The surrounding mountains cool the air and provide Vienna’s drinking water, while the valleys in between contain fertile land.

  • Space to grow: An abundance of vacant houses, commercial spaces and agricultural lots makes expansion affordable and welcomed by locals.

  • Connectivity: One hour by train to Vienna and 90 minutes to the airport position us right at the center of Europe’s rail and air connections.

With local conditions ripe and global pressures rising, it’s time to turn opportunity into action and start building. The future is shaped by the actions we take today.

From hub to valley

The commons hub already anchors this process. Battle-tested as an event venue and guesthouse, it hosts everything from collaborative finance conferences, solarpunk meetups, and activist gatherings to academic workshops and prototyping sessions. To an emerging Valley of the Commons, it provides:

  • An economic engine: providing jobs, visibility, and a constant stream of curious people seeking alternatives to the status quo;

  • A platform for entrepreneurship: supporting new event series, research projects, product prototyping, and startup incubation;

  • A beacon for metamodern thought and imagination: holding space for narratives that orient us beyond collapse.

Housing the future

A key pillar of the valley will be housing — not “smart homes” full of gadgets, but dwellings designed for the real challenges of the 21st century: climate change, resource constraints, and hyper-mobile lifestyles. We envision:

  • Renovated houses integrating state-of-the-art sustainable living concepts;

  • Cooperative ownership: from permanent co-housing to time-share models and shorter-term rentals;

  • Distributed governance: each house organized by its residents, following the principle of subsidiarity.

The commons hub GmbH is a pragmatic bootstrap, but the valley itself will be community-owned and self-governed. Our role is to provide initial momentum — network, knowledge, infrastructure, and capital — then step back.

Production and self-sufficiency

The Valley of the Commons won’t just be a place to live — it will be a place to collaboratively produce value in diverse ways:

  • Digital production in communal co-working spaces;

  • Physical production in co-owned FabLabs seeking to develop innovative niche products and providing local manufacturing for community needs;

  • Basic needs provision: 100% water and energy self-sufficiency asap, while gradually building food resilience through community farming.

In this way, production cycles will not only create a semi-autonomous local economy, but also build the capacity to provide for livelihoods and withstand future global disruptions.

Governance and community

A key challenge in the political realm consists of balancing local autonomy with collective coherence, while also rebalancing the relationship between capital and labor through cooperative ownership and participatory governance. Guided by the principle of subsidiarity, we envision:

  • Co-owned and self-governed houses and productive units;

  • Village-wide commons coordinated through collectively chosen mechanisms;

  • Integration with municipal politics based on mutual recognition and complementarity.

announcing: Popup Village 2026

For now, the Valley of the Commons remains a vision, inspired by conversations among commons-oriented networks, deep adaptation thinkers, and p2p communities preparing for civilizational transition. To make it real, it needs future commons villagers to step in.

In 2026, we plan a 4–6 week popup village — exploring housing, governance, production, and the valley itself, with the goal of turning vision into concrete plans.

Michel Bauwens, eminent Commons and P2P scholar, is on board, bringing his vision of a shift toward a commons-based civilization and experience with cosmo-local production. Veterans in mutual credit, community currencies, and housing coops are planning local research projects, while community leaders from Web3 co-livings and ecovillages provide guidance to help lay the foundations of the Valley of the Commons.

The organizing team includes veterans of Zuzalu and other “zu-villages.” Together, we will explore not only what is possible, but what it feels like to live in a valley oriented around the commons.

A growing campus, a growing commons

The immediate next step on this journey is the expansion of the hub into a monastery-like Event Campus capable of hosting summits, exhibitions, and popups. To make this happen, we are running a community lending campaign, raising €200k in loans from our network to secure and renovate the buildings. Over €80k have already been pledged, with some lenders even donating their interest back to support future events.

Supporting the church expansion lays the groundwork for the Valley of the Commons — the first step toward a campus that could grow into a vibrant village.

🌱 Lend to us – help bridge the final stretch of funding.

🙋‍♂️ Pre-register for the 2026 popup village.

✍️ Write to f.fritsch@commons-hub.at to get involved in the popup organization.

Together, we can turn vision into reality.
summary: Outline of our long-term goal of building a Valley of the Commons

title: commons hub going full cycle
body:
Life of a building

Four seasons have passed since the papers were signed and the commons hub was officially given its new name. So, I would like to take the time that my role and this season of death and reflection has granted me, to listen to the hub itself and try my best to communicate it’s perspective of the last year that it has; housed us, hosted our events, digested our waste, lighted our nights, resisted the elements, stood tall and strong.

 

My first cycle as the commons hub

I have lived many a decade over my hopefully short lifetime, during my time I have had seasons of sickness and disrepair, due to toxic human behavior and abandonment. However I have happily also hosted many a lively human and housed countless local critters within my aching bones.

It is the duty of my kind, and I accept this burden with great honor and purpose. Nothing makes me more anxious, than to think, that I would be abandoned again and left without life within my hollows.

 

winter

I was very grateful after some turbulent years, that last winter, the current human inhabitants chose to nest within me. They had cleared out a destructive bout of indigestion I suffered earlier in the season and decorated my degraded rooms with love and care. Which brought to me a renewed sense of hope, as I was beginning to fear complete abandonment and a quick degeneration,

to an ultimate ending off my beingness.

 

spring

The humans then began attracting others to further my regeneration, both from with in and out my boundaries. So, my inner space became further orderly and healed from the disease I had picked up last winter. The regions surrounding my structure, where the plant kind eternally encroached upon my membrane walls, were cleared and I felt space to breathe fully again. Ahh, such a relief it was! Also, I received a colon cleansing and my bowels were renewed. Oh, what a blessing that was! The chaos, which I had endured for some years previously, had been soothed with the caring attention of my nesting humans, and through their aliveness they cultivated seeds of the plant kind withing my liver room where they usually just drank and smoked. I had enthusiasm for the future once again. As I believed that the humans were here to stay, to become,

my humans.

 

summer

So, as the season of warmth and abundance approached, I was feeling an aliveness and strength that I hadn’t felt in many years. My humans attracted even more humans to come and celebrate their lives within me. Ah such joy! The strange noises that reverberated from my inner spaces out, had given me a great voice that filled the valley where I was born. With this magnificent voice I felt like a grand instrument of music, a privilege that the others of my kind who sadly spend much of their time quiet by their humans, know little about. I was loud and noticeable! Also, many strange but inviting odors emanated from my stomach room and gave spiciness to my normal smell. The buzzing of the many humans within, vibrated through my bones and I felt high with the abundance of life energy. I felt that I could blast off and float with my humans into the space surrounding the Motherhouse, to explore the other Greathomes spinning around the Centrelight! Wow, that was an intense time! Soo much change and interaction I began to worry, wondering if it would ever calm down. But at the same time, I didn’t want it to. I was party, I was gathering,

I was ALIVE!

 

Autumn

As the season of the fall came around, the humans were steadily coming and going. The celebrations were of all kinds and sizes; I was so intrigued by all the various groupings that had celebrated within me. There were an ebb and flow of human activity within me, that I remember having a creeping fear whether my aging body could handle all this action. Thankfully my humans had not just used and abandoned me like the earlier inhabitants, I could feel their continued presence and care for me and I began to believe that they had (and still have) love for me. However, all the action had taken its toll and some of my internal systems were becoming problematic,

fear crept in.

 

Winter again

So full circle we come back to the dark and cold season of snow and harsh winds. As the snow began to fall a mass influx of humans came and I was overwhelmed. My heat circulation shut down, and I felt too weak to accommodate a group of this size for so long. I was scared that I wouldn’t be able to handle it. Thankfully I survived, as did the humans, and I have been slowly recovering as the human flow began to fade out. I still feel the love from my humans and have faith that they will continue to rejuvenate my ageing body with their care and attention, and for this I will return the love and continue to stand strong and pledge my strength, to protect my humans and their friends from the elements, for I wish many seasons and cycles to share,

with my new family.

 

thank you for sharing your lives with me

your home

the commons hub

 

No, thank you!

for holding us while we try our best to get along

for taking our disregard and excesses

being unfailingly there so as to be taken for granted

for protecting us from the elements

for hopefully hosting many generations to come

love you commons hub, ❤️D
summary:
one year ago the commons hub was signed over! 
happy birthday commons hub, may you be for another 1000 years!

title: Come survive the european winter with us
body:
Winter Co-Living

Need a place to get away for a month or two? Do you want to live in a winter wonderland where glorious mountains hikes begin from the front door? Want a peaceful place far from the city mess and noise but not too far that you can get back in an hour with one train?

what/where/when

We have an old Gasthaus at the mouth of Höllental between two great mountains that we have renovated to host events, parties, conferences and all sorts of gatherings, however as we have no events planned for, until the end of March, we will take this opportunity for further renovations and to prepare for the upcoming year. Therefore we have some empty rooms which we would like to fill with interesting people who would like a month or two to live with us.

who

So, who are we? Daniel is a 40 yo aussie settled permahippyrainbowninjatraveler who has found himself in the downsideup land where strange things are happening; Emil and Felix, two brothers running this project since 2023 are around from time to time for work and to go climbing and hiking; and then there is a 30 something yo old soul who is the picture of health and calmness, who is an inspiration to the rest of us without being an arsehole about it; and not least a local cat who will cuddle with anyone who’s willing to sit on the couch long enough; a small trickle of outside guests (e.g. hikers or weekend getaways, usually a nice couple or a pair of friends) and potentially you?

Price

Rooms range from €500-600 per month, all utilities, internet, etc included. You're free to use our fablab and event space too, it might be a little cold in there but lots of stuff to do!

contact

If you're intrigued but wanna know more, have a look at www.commons-hub.at , or have a video call (ger/eng) with us!
summary: We opening up the possibility to rent one of the dorm rooms as a private room for month long stays from now until end of March 2026

title: Hack the Hub 2026
body:
Hack the Hub!

27 March to 07 April, 2026

(pic) need to get a sprout coming out of snow picture!

The snow is starting to melt, the first inklings of spring are manifesting, and the garden is waking up from hibernation.

It's time to Hack the Hub again!

Same as last year, we're calling on friends and supporters of the Hub to flock to Reichenau over Easter, lend their hands during day and celebrate the birth of a new cycle at night. We offer a straightup energy exchange - 4 hrs of active work per day for food and bed while you stay.

Lots of projects big and small are already in planning, even if we just achieve half of them the Hub will shine as never before. As always, we are open to suggestions and the serendipity of our flow, but we do want to prioritize finsihable projects that give you the happiness of completing something and witnessing the difference that you co-created!

What to do

There is much to do in the garden, as is always the case, and we would like as many strong backs with green thumbs as possible to come. We could also benefit from construction/tool use skills, good eyes for design and shui and cooking abilities. However, anyone with enthusiasm and a willingness to learn is welcome.

Side back garden

The side garden bed will need to be prepared for tomatoes and then planted.

The big box to be prepared and planted with crawling plants (e.g. pumpkin, sweet potato and watermelon)

The small box with root plants (e.g. potato, garlic, onion)

And if you allow me to dream....

....making a living fence with arch doorway separating the back side garden from the main section of the backyard and then planting the climbing plants.

Compost corner

The compost needs some turning action, that means a lot of f*rking shoveling! Then we will cover the new heap and prepare a new compost cage and material store areas. 

Back fence remake

Removing a section of the fence and clearing the area of plants 

Wall facelifts

The bathroom block facade needs a good puttying! Would be a big boost to insulation!

While we are at it and for those with fear of heights, we can putty the kitchen facade as well.

The courtyard facade also could use some love, the windows require a fine touch and artisanal competencies (which we don’t have...) 

Courtyard playground

Attaching a pole horizontally to the crown of the Linden tree, so that swings and ropes can be attached.

So if we are going to dream then I would like to make ninja steps to the crown where a platform is! 

Commons gym

We would like to create a community gym that will be open for all to use. We plan to hang various equipment (rings, climber’s balls, trapeze and rope/silks), set up bolt and pole for a slackline, move the crash mat a little and beautify the open courtyard nearby (see below).

If we are to continue to dream a small climbing wall that leans over the mat. 

Museum courtyard

This area could be so much more! First, clearing the space of the wood (i.e. bon fire anyone?) and dealing with the massive cement blocks! I am thinking of filling the space with antique farming equipment, which we fill with earth and flowers - this time of season I would suggest Nasturtiums and wild poppies. But all flowering kind would be welcome. Then we can setup chairs and tables when needed.

Still in the dreamworld... it would be amazing to pour the area map cement model and place it somewhere in this space! 

Museum gardens

The area behind the museum and courtyard could use some intelligent permaculture style design implementations. Something like a dedicated wood and grass compost area, living fences for camping potential and some tree root removal. 

This little side area could be cleared and those wagons used in some interesting way.

Bike shed cut-del-paste

Would be good to clear out the whole room and reintroduce the bikes with associated tools and materials to maintain them. 

Hack the Tub!

Last but not least is our beloved hot tub. This tub has warmed many a commoner while they shared music, ideas, drinks and bodily fluids. It’s the liquidity pool that shares it all!

The good old tub has unfortunately cooked its last commoner last year ☹ ! But don't you weep, we'll buy a new tub, to be set up during the Hack! Then, while it is filling and heating up, we plan on extending the stone platform to the right of the tub, and generall improve the area around the tub. With all this done we can inaugurate the new tub and enjoy directly the fruits of our labor with a well deserved.

What to bring

The spring time here can be chaotic and the temperature can fluctuate from blissful warm sunshine to flash snow! So we suggest you bring:

  • Work shoes (e.g. gumboots, throwaway shoes)

  • Warm clothes (I think one heavy coat should suffice)

  • House slippers (we would be happy to keep them after 😽)

  • Your best!

 contact

If any of this is tingling the part of you that gets excited then please fill out the sign up form here and prepare yourself to co creatively rejuvenate the hub and self! I’ll be there with a tool in my hand and a smile on my face.
summary: Come and share in the spring rejuvenation of the hub before we welcome in the summer season

title: Time for awakenings and preparation
body:
I have been outside, finally, after a spell of heavy cloudage and have begun to detect signage of sprinage in the garten!

I present some videos of the current situation at the hub right now (few hours from now…). Feel free to watch and share or even edit, whatever!

Soon no more sleighing!

 

The birds are returning!

The garden is awakening!

 

waking slowly after a long sleep

I invite us all, me, brothers and sisters, mother and fathers, aunties and uncles, nieces and nephews, the matriarchs and yes, the patriarchs too, all! To take an opportunity this moment of natural re-awakening we collectively refer to as spring, to engage with the seeds beginning to sprout withus and detect the flowers we would like this summer to bloom outfrom us and into the future collective gardens we wish to live in, with each other. Spend as much time, now, in any space with plant life emerging from the great sleep we call winter and witness the awakening of new seeds introduced into the patch of earth last summer to begin to sprout, break through to see some sunlight and to potentially grow a new plant, you had never experienced before, grow within you and be shared amongst your companion patches… who knows what will grow when we give a little space and tender care to the falling of last summer’s seeds. Maybe a beautiful symbiotic garden can grow, with abundance for the diversity of expressions to manifest greatness for all.

 A place I would like to live in, with you.

 

preparing for the big sleep and tropical storms

To my southern hemispherically situated everyone and to the tropical coconuts and papaya peoples around the world’s waist, I propose a taking of the transitional moments facing y#all now, to fall with faith, clear space and open too long closed windows and allow yourselves to breath out the trapped negative energy, out into the cold to die with the plants. For the tropical brothers and sisters, to take this moment to allow the stagnant waters to flow downstream to the ocean to be assimilated by the underwater world to feed the symbiotic cycle between our two worlds that the Earth has provided, may the storms of re-creation be awesome and not awful… I pray that the chaos and destructive force of the Earth can be survived by our southern compatriots with the abundance that the north in summer can provide and is allowed to flow.

I hope that the opening of a good and abundant northern spring can lead to a true reversal of the closing and aggressive and violent trends we see emerging around and through us, as too be able balance such forces with a open sharing of space, to host and shelter the adventurous, cold, trapped, scared, dying southern tribe members in our time of abundance, so that next time we northern dwelling folk face the season of death we are welcome! Yes, rather than resented…

Lastly for my subtropical family. so jealous am i, of the abundance and consistency of good weather. please continue to protect and hold that glorious space for the refugees of every sort from both hemispheres to recharge, release and regenerate.

All in all I wish you all survive and/or thrive this challenging intense inspiring expiring season of transition, with the much necessary deep changes happening around and through you, that it brings and takes.  (❤️) (🐈‍⬛)
